event.text: Have you noticed any drainage, pus, warmth, or streaking from the wound, or any spreading of the redness?
event.why: Presence of purulence or rapid progression would indicate need for urgent evaluation and possible systemic antibiotics or drainage; these findings help distinguish cellulitis severity and guide whether outpatient versus inpatient care is needed.

event.text: I recommend being seen in person today (urgent care, your diabetes/foot clinic, or a same-day podiatry or primary care slot) for a foot wound in a person with diabetes that is now red, swollen and tender. Someone needs to look at the wound directly. If you cannot get an in-person slot today, go to urgent care or an emergency department. Go sooner if you develop fever or chills, spreading redness or red streaks, pus, black or dusky skin, or rapidly increasing pain. You can also ask a Counsel clinician to review this thread, but don't let that delay the visit.
